summary: The root لفح (lfH) primarily describes fire or hot wind (سموم) striking or smiting a face, causing a burning sensation. It can also mean to strike lightly with a sword.
lane: 1 لَفَحَتْهُ النَّارُ ذ , (S, M, K,) aor. لَفَحَ , (M,) inf. n. لَفْحٌ and لَفَحَانٌ , (M, K,) The fire smote, or hurt, his face; as also لفحت وَجْهَهُ : (M, O:) the fire burned him; (TA;) as also نفحته النار بِحَرِّهَا ; (S, K;) and in like manner the hot wind called سَمُوم : (S:) لَفَحَتْ and نَفَحَتْ are syn., except that the effect of النَّفْح is greater than that of اللَّفْح : (Zj:) or لَفْحٌ relates to a hot wind; and نَفْحٌ , to a cold, or cool, wind: (As, S:) you also say لفحته السَّمُوم meaning the سموم blew in his face. (L.) -b2- Also لَفَحَهُ , aor. لَفَحَ , He smote, or struck, him, with a sword, (S, K,) lightly, or slightly: you say لَفَحْتُهُ بِالسَّيْفِ لَفْحَةً I struck him with the sword a light, or slight, blow. (S.)

headwords.def: لَفَحَتْهُ النَّارُ , (S, M, K,) aor. لَفَحَ, (M,) inf. n. لَفْحٌ and لَفَحَانٌ, (M, K,) The fire smote, or hurt, his face; as also لفحت وَجْهَهُ: (M, O:) the fire burned him; (TA;) as also نفحته النار بِحَرِّهَا; (S, K;) and in like manner the hot wind called سَمُوم: (S:) لَفَحَتْ and نَفَحَتْ are syn., except that the effect of النَّفْح is greater than that of اللَّفْح: (Zj:) or لَفْحٌ relates to a hot wind; and نَفْحٌ, to a cold, or cool, wind: (As, S:) you also say لفحته السَّمُوم…

أَصَابَهَ لفْحٌ مِنْ حَرُورٍ وَسَمُومٍ A burning gust of hot night-wind, and of hot day-wind, smote him. (L.) أَصَابَهُ مِنَ الحَرِّ لَفْحٌ وَمِنَ البَرْدِ نَفْحٌ [ A blast of heat smote him, and a blast of cold ]. (A.) You say also لَوَافِحُ السَّمُوِم [pl. of, and meaning Burning blasts of the سموم ]. (S, K in art. سفع.)
A light, or slight, blow with a sword. (S.)

A certain well known plant, (K,) of the kind termed يَقْطِينِىٌّ, (L,) which people smell, (S.) yellow, and of sweet odour, (A, L,) resembling the بَا ِنْجَان (S, A, K,) when it becomes yellow; (S, A;) [accord. to Golius, app. on the authority of Ibn-Beytár, the same which the Syrians and Egyptians call شَمَّامٌ, q. v.].

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
